questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Ukraine?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter K and has 4 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Kyiv.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Ukraine?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter B and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: It borders Russia, Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Moldova.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Ukraine?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter U and has 9 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language” part of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: The official language of Ukraine is Ukrainian (Ukrainian: українська мова, [ukrajin’s’ka mova]).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ seized Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Volyn Lands.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter L and has 9 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Kyivan Rus” part of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: Lithuania seized Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Volyn Lands.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was one of only two INES level 7 accidents (the worst level) in the history of nuclear power, the other being the Fukushima nuclear disaster in _____.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter J and has 5 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “20th century” part of the Ukraine article.

questions.proof: It was one of only two INES level 7 accidents (the worst level) in the history of nuclear power, the other being the Fukushima nuclear disaster in Japan.
